objective.statement: Know the four families of the orchestra, their main instruments, their clefs and which play highest and lowest.
successCriteria: I know the strings, woodwind, brass and percussion.
I know the usual clef of each instrument.
I know which instrument of a family plays the highest and the lowest notes.

explanation.text: The orchestra has four groups of instruments: strings, woodwind, brass and percussion. The standard strings are the violin, viola, cello and double bass. The standard woodwind are the flute, oboe, clarinet and bassoon. The standard brass are the trumpet, horn, trombone and tuba.

Within each family the instruments are listed from the one that can play the highest notes to the one that can play the lowest: violin to double bass, flute to bassoon, trumpet to tuba. Smaller instruments play higher.

Each instrument has a clef it normally uses; others may be used if the music goes very high or low. The violin, flute, oboe, clarinet, trumpet and horn normally read the treble clef. The cello, bassoon, trombone, double bass and tuba normally read the bass clef. The viola normally reads the alto clef.

music.textAlternative: An alto stave with middle C, G and E: a few notes for the viola.

explanation.caption: The viola reads the alto clef.

explanation.text: The percussion family includes the timpani (kettle drums), the side drum, the bass drum and the cymbals. Of these, only the timpani produce notes of definite pitch; they are tuned to particular notes, often the tonic and the dominant of the key.
Four families: strings, woodwind, brass, percussion. Treble clef for the high instruments, bass clef for the low ones, alto clef for the viola. Only the timpani have definite pitch.

provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 18 and First Steps Grade 4 section 15 (p. 102, read in the PDF): the four groups, the standard instruments of each, highest-to-lowest order, normal clefs and the pitched timpani. The book underlines the clefs an instrument ALWAYS uses; the underlining could not be read reliably from the scan, so the course says 'normally' everywhere (TEACHER TO CONFIRM). Transposing instruments are Grade 5 and are never asked.
